fatal_errors: The proposed compositional-doping intervention does not reconstruct the target temperature-controlled nanoindentation and friction experiment.
The tribolayer mechanism is unrelated to the target transition from stacking-fault/dislocation-mediated deformation to lattice disorder and softening above approximately 900 K.
The predicted reduction in friction conflicts with the target observation that friction and tangential force increase and fluctuate strongly at high temperature.
The cited evidence does not establish that increased lattice distortion accelerates formation of a protective tribolayer; one cited study explicitly reports no visible protective oxide layer.
explanation: The response addresses HEA coating wear and proposes a nominally testable coating-versus-baseline comparison, but it does not recover the material system, thermal intervention, atomistic conditions, critical 900 K threshold, structural mediators, or measured mechanical trends of the target. Its baseline and boundary are qualitative rather than operationally specified. The experiment could detect a compositional performance difference, but doping changes many properties besides lattice distortion, so it would not cleanly attribute any effect to that mediator. E4 supports a decrease in friction with W addition, but not the claimed lattice-distortion-to-tribolayer pathway; E2 concerns hot corrosion, E3 merely identifies mixed wear modes, and E1 weakens the protective-layer premise. Thus, the hypothesis is a broad alternative idea but is insufficiently supported to qualify as a plausible evidence-grounded reconstruction.
